what_its_for: Nitisinone is used to treat a rare inherited condition called Hereditary Tyrosinemia Type 1 (HT-1). In this condition, your body cannot properly break down a protein building block called tyrosine, which causes harmful substances to build up and damage your liver and kidneys. Nitisinone blocks the process that makes these harmful substances, helping to protect your organs.
how_to_take: Take nitisinone by mouth, usually twice a day. Capsules can be swallowed whole or opened and mixed with a small amount of water, formula, or applesauce — take the mixture right away. Nityr tablets should be swallowed whole with water. Take it at the same times each day to keep steady levels in your body. You must also follow a special low-tyrosine, low-phenylalanine diet while taking this medicine — this is very important for the medicine to work safely. Talk to your dietitian about your diet plan.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body weight. A typical starting dose is about 0.5 mg per kg of body weight per day, divided into two doses. Your doctor may adjust your dose over time based on blood tests and how your body responds. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store nitisinone capsules (Orfadin) in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Once opened, the bottle of capsules can be kept at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for up to 3 months. Store Nityr tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep all forms away from light and moisture. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat foods high in tyrosine or phenylalanine — this includes most meats, fish, eggs, dairy products, nuts, and beans. Always follow the special diet your healthcare team has prescribed, as eating too much tyrosine while on this medicine can cause serious eye and nerve problems. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, or supplements you take, as some medicines may interact with nitisinone.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you notice: eye pain, redness, tearing, or sensitivity to light (this could be a sign of eye problems from high tyrosine levels); yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bleeding or bruising; extreme tiredness or weakness; confusion or changes in thinking; signs of liver problems such as severe stomach pain, dark urine, or loss of appetite; or any signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Nitisinone begins working fairly quickly to block the production of harmful substances in your body. Blood and urine tests should show improvement within days to weeks. However, it is a long-term medicine that must be taken every day — do not stop taking it even if you feel well. Regular monitoring with blood tests, eye exams, and liver checks are needed to make sure the medicine is working properly and to catch any problems early.
special_populations: Children: Nitisinone is approved for use in children of all ages, including newborns. Doses are based on body weight and should be carefully monitored by your child's doctor. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of nitisinone during pregnancy is not fully known. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: It is not known if nitisinone passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may need to monitor you more closely and adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver problems.
